children.text: Mistral zero data retention, DPA and training

By default Mistral keeps API inputs and outputs for 30 rolling days to monitor abuse. Zero data retention (ZDR) is available on pay-as-you-go for stateless API calls, and Mistral approves requests case by case. In free mode, Mistral may train on your API inputs and outputs unless you opt out. For pay-as-you-go, Mistral does not state a default, only that you can opt out at any time. So turn training off in the admin Privacy settings before you send it meeting transcripts. This page also covers what the Mistral DPA commits to.

Mistral's training default
Mistral's defaults depend on the plan, and one of them is not written down.
Free mode (Mistral AI Studio): Mistral says it may use your API inputs and outputs to train its models. You can opt out at any time.

Pay-as-you-go: Mistral's help center says customers "retain full control over this processing and have the right to opt out at any time". It does not say whether training is on or off before you touch the setting.
Feedback: rating a response with thumbs up or down lets Mistral use that rating, and the input and output, to train its models on every plan.

Mistral's commercial terms (effective 25 September 2026) say it will not use customer data or outputs to train its models except when you opted in on a product that is opt-out by default, or did not opt out on a product that is opt-in by default. Because the API default is not stated, the safe step is to switch training off yourself: in the admin console, open Privacy and disable the "Anonymous improvement data" toggle. Mistral's API toggle and its Vibe (consumer app) toggle are separate, so opting out of one does not opt you out of the other.
When Meetily users select Mistral as their summary provider via BYOK, the request goes to the Mistral API under your API key, and your account's settings apply.
Retention

For the standard APIs, Mistral keeps your Input and Output for the time needed to generate the Output and then for 30 rolling days to monitor abuse, after which it is deleted, unless zero data retention is activated. Two API paths store data longer: the Agents API retains data until you terminate your account, and the Fine-Tuning API retains it until you delete it from Mistral AI Studio or terminate your account.

Mistral's consumer chat app, Vibe (formerly Le Chat), keeps conversations until you delete them or your account, and is out of scope for this page. For the binding text, consult the current privacy policy and DPA on legal.mistral.ai before deployment in regulated environments.
Zero data retention
Zero data retention is available, but it is scoped:
Plan: pay-as-you-go only.

Endpoints: stateless API calls only: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/fim/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/moderations, /v1/ocr, and /v1/audio/. Agents, batch processing, the Files API, and Vibe are not covered.
How: submit a request through Mistral's Help Center or support team with your reasons. Mistral approves requests at its discretion.
When ZDR is on, the 30-day abuse-monitoring window does not apply.
Where your data is processed

Mistral is a French company and its DPA is written around GDPR, but EU processing is not the default. For the global endpoint, api.mistral.ai, Mistral says it does not commit to a specific inference location.
Regional inference is available as an option:
api.eu.mistral.ai for the EU, and api.us.mistral.ai for the US.
Regional endpoints cost 1.1 times standard list pricing.
They support function calling, but not other tool calls or stateful features (agents, batch, the Files API), and some models may not be offered in every region.
Account configuration, API keys, billing, and usage data may still be handled outside the chosen region. Only the inference step is regional.
What the Mistral DPA says
Mistral's Data Processing Addendum (effective 27 July 2026) is the contract that governs personal data in your API traffic. Three points matter for meeting transcripts:

Training: the DPA lets Mistral act as controller to train its models "in accordance with its Privacy Policy, unless Customer is or has opted-out of training". Opting out in the admin console is what removes this.
Feedback: thumbs up or down feedback, with the associated input and output, is used to train Mistral's models.
Abuse monitoring: automated moderation, including abuse monitoring on the APIs, applies except when zero data retention is active.
How Meetily uses Mistral

Meetily routes Mistral traffic through your own API key. Your account's contract terms and privacy settings apply. The transcript text is sent over TLS to the Mistral API for summarization, and the response is returned to Meetily and stored locally on your device. Audio is never transmitted to Mistral at any point.

Before you connect Mistral, switch training off in the admin console and, if your organization needs it, request zero data retention. For zero retention by construction, switch to local Ollama and keep the entire pipeline on-device.

Frequently asked questions
Does Mistral train models on my API prompts? (free vs pay-as-you-go)

It depends on the plan, and Mistral does not state every default. In free mode on Mistral AI Studio, Mistral says it may use your API inputs and outputs to train its models, and you can opt out at any time. For pay-as-you-go, Mistral's help center says only that customers retain full control over this processing and can opt out at any time; it does not say whether training is on or off by default. Mistral's commercial terms say it will not train on customer data unless you opted in, or did not opt out of a product that is opt-in by default. Feedback you give with the thumbs up or down buttons is used for training on every plan. For meeting transcripts, turn training off in the Privacy section of the admin console before you connect Mistral to Meetily.
What is the default retention period for Mistral API traffic?

For the standard APIs, Mistral keeps your Input and Output for the time needed to generate the Output and then for 30 rolling days to monitor abuse, unless zero data retention is activated. Two exceptions store data longer: the Agents API keeps data until you terminate your account, and the Fine-Tuning API keeps fine-tuning data until you delete it or terminate your account. Mistral's consumer chat app, Vibe (formerly Le Chat), has separate terms and is out of scope for this page.
Is zero data retention available for Mistral?

Yes, but it is scoped. ZDR is available only with pay-as-you-go and only for stateless API calls: chat completions, FIM completions, embeddings, moderations, OCR, and audio. It does not cover agents, batch processing, the Files API, or Vibe. You request it through Mistral's Help Center or support team, explain your reasons, and Mistral approves requests at its discretion. When ZDR is active, the 30-day abuse-monitoring window does not apply.
Where is Mistral API data processed geographically?

Not in a guaranteed location by default. Mistral's documentation says it does not commit to an inference location for requests sent to the global endpoint, api.mistral.ai. For EU-only inference, use the regional endpoint api.eu.mistral.ai, which costs 1.1 times standard pricing and supports function calling but not agents, batch, or the Files API. Even then, account settings, API keys, billing, and usage data may be handled outside the region.
How do I request deletion of data Mistral has retained?
Submit a deletion request per the procedures in Mistral's DPA. Account-level deletion is also available through the Mistral admin console.
Does Mistral have SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certifications?
Mistral publishes its compliance posture on legal.mistral.ai and in its Help Center. Check the current certifications list before deployment in regulated environments.
How does Meetily handle Mistral when I pick it as my summary provider?

Meetily transcription runs 100% locally by default. When you select a Mistral model as your summary provider via BYOK, Meetily routes transcript text (not audio) to the Mistral API using your own key. The retention and training defaults on this page apply to your traffic.
Is Mistral a good choice for EU customers under GDPR?

It can be, with care. Mistral is a French company with a GDPR-based DPA, but EU processing is not the default: requests to api.mistral.ai have no committed location. Use the EU endpoint, api.eu.mistral.ai, if you need inference to stay in the EU, and note that account and billing data may still be handled outside the region.

Meetily transcription stays 100% local by default. For summaries, bring your own Mistral AI key (BYOK) so the data path matches the policy you just read - or pick a local model if you want zero retention by construction.
